sink: fetch() to JungleBus API with caller string spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: txid is an optional free-form string (no format check, unlike bsv_decodeTransaction's isTxid regex) concatenated raw into the path. A value containing '/' and '..' segments (e.g. '../../v1/other') is normalized by the URL/fetch parser and can replace the entire '/transaction/get/' prefix, letting the caller redirect the request to any other path on the fixed junglebusUrl() host with no validation at all. Impact is capped because the host is fixed (server-configured) and no secret headers are attached on this call, so I flag Tier B rather than A.
contract: App-only: fetches BSV price, chain info, decodes transactions, and looks up addresses.

why: the optional query string is only ever passed into OneSatServices.market.searchListings, whose MarketClient/BaseClient.buildQueryString (node_modules/@1sat/client 0.0.51) runs encodeURIComponent on every value before appending it to the fixed baseUrl, so no path/query injection is possible.

sink: fetch() to the GorillaPool ordinals API with caller string spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: address is a required free-form string with no format validation (not checked against a Bitcoin-address regex) and is concatenated raw into the request path with zero encoding. A '../'-laden address value normalizes past the '/txos/address/.../unspent' prefix and can redirect the request to any other path on the fixed legacyOrdinalsUrl() host. Tier B because the target host is fixed/public and no credentials ride on this request, limiting real impact.
contract: App-only: scans a Bitcoin address for categorized UTXOs — funding, ordinals, and BSV-21 tokens.

why: idKey is only ever sent as a JSON field inside a POST body (fetchProfile in tools/bap/getId.ts) to the fixed BSOCIAL_API_URL, never interpolated into a URL, shell, or file path, so there is no injection sink.

sink: fetch() to the BMAP API with bapId spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: bapId is a required free-form string with no validation, concatenated raw into the path ahead of the fixed 'endpoint' segment. A traversal-laden bapId (e.g. containing '../') is normalized by the URL parser and can replace the '/bap/<id>/' prefix entirely, letting the caller redirect the GET request to any other path on the fixed BMAP_URL host. Tier B: fixed public host, no credentials attached, GET-only, so concrete exploit value beyond 'query a different BMAP endpoint yourself' is unproven.
contract: Read follow relationships from the BMAP API. Shows who a user is following or who follows them.

sink: fetch() to the BMAP API with txid spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: txid is a required free-form string with no hex/length validation, concatenated raw into the path ahead of the fixed '/like' segment. A traversal value in txid escapes the intended path and can retarget the request to an arbitrary path on the same fixed BMAP_URL host. Tier B for the same reasons as bmap_readFollows (fixed public host, no attached secrets, GET only).
contract: Read likes and reactions for a specific post from the BMAP API. Shows who liked the post and what emoji reactions were used.

sink: fetch() to the BMAP API with txid spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: When txid is supplied it is concatenated raw into the path with no validation, letting a traversal-laden value redirect the GET request to any other path on the fixed BMAP_URL host (the bapId/address filters in the list branch are safely encoded via URLSearchParams, so this applies only to the single-post txid branch). Tier B: fixed public host, no credentials, GET only.
contract: Read social posts from the BMAP API (query layer). Can fetch posts by author (BAP ID), specific post by transaction ID, or recent posts from all users. Supports pagination and feed functionality.

sink: fetch() to the BMAP API with txid spliced unescaped into the URL path
why: Identical pattern to bmap_readPosts: an unvalidated txid is concatenated raw into the path in the single-post branch, letting a traversal value redirect the GET request elsewhere on the fixed BMAP_URL host. Tier B for the same fixed-host/no-credential reasons.
contract: Read social posts from the BSV blockchain using BMAP API. Can fetch posts by author (BAP ID), specific post by transaction ID, or recent posts from all users. Supports pagination and feed functionality.

why: registered with inputSchema z.object({}) (server.ts ~351) and the handler takes no arguments at all, so there is no caller-controlled input to reach any sink.

the only value ever spliced into the JungleBus fetch URL (tools/bsv/decodeTransaction.ts fetchJungleBusData) is either the SDK-computed transaction.hash('hex') (not caller data) or the caller's tx string after it has passed isTxid()'s strict /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i check; the raw-tx path instead runs through @bsv/sdk Transaction.fromBinary/fromHex, a structured bitcoin-transaction parser, not a generic deserializer or command/URL sink.

sink: explorerFetch() to the configured explorer API with the caller string spliced unescaped into the URL path
guard: partial: only enforced when EXPLORER_API_KEY is set
why: blockHash/txHash/address are free-form strings (no format validation) spliced raw into apiUrl. explorerFetch() (utils/backends.ts) only checks that the resulting URL stays under the explorer's path prefix, and only when process.env.EXPLORER_API_KEY is set -- if that env var is unset (the default; no fallback value is defined), the entire origin/prefix check is skipped and the traversal-laden request is sent unchecked. I cannot confirm from static code whether a given deployment sets EXPLORER_API_KEY, so this is config-dependent -- Tier B. Even when the key is set, the check runs on the already-normalized URL, so it appears effective in that case.
contract: Explore Bitcoin SV blockchain data using the configured explorer API...

outpoint is rejected unless it matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}[._]\d+$/i (tools/ordinals/getInscription.ts) before being passed to services.ordfs.getMetadata, so no character that could alter the request path or method ever reaches the OrdfsClient.

id is rejected unless it matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}[._]\d+$/i (tools/ordinals/getTokenByIdOrTicker.ts) before being passed to services.bsv21.getTokenDetails, so no injection-capable character ever reaches the Bsv21Client path segment.

q/type/limit/from are passed straight into OneSatServices.market.searchListings, and MarketClient/BaseClient.buildQueryString (node_modules/@1sat/client 0.0.51) runs encodeURIComponent on every value before building the query string, so no path or query injection is possible.

data/from/to only drive @bsv/sdk's Utils.toArray/toHex/toBase64/toUTF8 encoding conversions or a plain JSON.parse into a number array (tools/utils/conversion.ts); the result is returned as text and never reaches a file, shell, URL, or eval sink.

query is only used locally to tokenize and score cached skill entries (tools/utils/findSkills.ts matchSkills/scoreSkill); it never reaches the fetch call, which always targets the hardcoded FIND_SKILLS_INDEX_URL, and every field of the fetched catalog is bounds-checked and allow-listed to raw.githubusercontent.com by isAllowedSkillUrl before being returned.

the only input is method, an enum of 3 fixed literals (tools/utils/installAgentMaster.ts) that merely selects a branch; the spawn("go", ["install", "github.com/b-open-io/agent-master-cli@latest"], {shell:true}) argument list is entirely hardcoded and never incorporates caller-controlled data, so there is no command-injection surface despite shell:true.
registered with an empty input schema (tools/wallet/onboarding.ts walletOnboardingInputSchema = z.object({})); the handler takes no arguments at all, so there is no caller-controlled input.

url/method/body/headers are fully caller-controlled and forwarded to X402Client.request (utils/x402.ts), but every outbound call goes through this repo's own serviceFetch (utils/x402-http.ts), which requires https-only with no embedded credentials/fragment, resolves DNS itself and rejects the request unless every resolved address is a public IP (explicitly excluding 0.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10 CGNAT, 198.18-19/16, multicast/class-E, and non-2000::/3 IPv6), pins the TCP connection to that pre-checked address (no DNS-rebinding window), and refuses to follow redirects; reserved headers (host/cookie/x402-*/payment-*/x-bsv-*) are also stripped by safeHeaders. I read this guard in the repo's own utils/x402-http.ts (not a dependency) and found no bypass for the default code path actually wired into registerX402Tools (no custom fetcher override).
